name: Recruit Training Command, Great Lakes
explanation: Enlisted boot camp for the Navy, at Naval Station Great Lakes, Illinois. Started 30 June 1997 and ended nine weeks later. The JST school window is 1 July 1997 to 5 September 1997.
civilian: This is where a new sailor learns to live in the Navy before going on to a technical school.

name: USS Tortuga (LSD-46)
explanation: A Whidbey Island-class dock landing ship. It carries Marines with their vehicles and landing craft, and launches the craft from a well deck that floods. Assault Craft Unit 4 (ACU 4) was the exercise partner on this TAD. Between the end of boot camp, 5 September 1997, and the start of Tech Core, 21 January 1998.
civilian: A ship that carries Marines and their boats and vehicles to a beach. ACU 4 was the exercise partner that ran the landing craft.

name: USS Essex (LHD-2)
explanation: A Wasp-class amphibious assault ship. Stop recorded at San Francisco, CA. Homeported at Naval Station San Diego (32nd Street) in that period. Dates for this stop have not been entered.
civilian: A big amphibious assault ship with a flight deck and a well deck for landing craft.
open: USS Essex (LHD-2): San Francisco stop; dates not entered.

name: Naval Training Center Great Lakes
explanation: The Navy's training center at Great Lakes, Illinois. Started after the USS Tortuga (LSD-46) TAD, in the first quarter of 1998, and ran through December 1998. The emblem shown is the seal of Naval Station Great Lakes, the installation's current name.
civilian: The Navy's big training base north of Chicago.

name: Naval Computer and Telecommunications Station San Diego
explanation: A shore command that ran Navy computer and telecommunications services in San Diego. Signum lists the NEC for this tour as 1589, calibration.
civilian: A land-based communications station, not a ship.

name: USS Frank Cable (AS-40)
explanation: A submarine tender: a ship that repairs, supplies, and houses the crews of submarines. In these years her home port was Guam. The NEC on Signum for this tour is 1589. The three Navy E awards dated 2001, 2002, and 2003 fall in this tour.
civilian: A repair ship for submarines, not a submarine itself.

name: EOD Mobile Unit Five
explanation: Explosive Ordnance Disposal Mobile Unit Five, a Navy bomb-disposal unit then based in Guam. Assignment to the unit is not the same as being a bomb-disposal technician. Signum lists the NEC as 9613, a communications specialty. The Royal Thai Navy hosted Cobra Gold in 2004 and 2005. An Australian CDT was the partner on Talisman Saber in 2005 and 2007.
civilian: The command's job was disposing of explosives. His recorded specialty there was communications.

name: Combined Joint Task Force Troy
explanation: A joint and coalition task force in Iraq in 2006, during Operation Iraqi Freedom, stood up against roadside bombs. EOD Mobile Unit 11 was the partner. The 52nd Ordnance Group and the 16th Engineer Brigade were sponsors. The Iraq campaign phase named for this tour is National Resolution.
civilian: A temporary headquarters in Iraq, drawn from more than one country and more than one branch.

name: 52nd Ordnance Group (EOD)
explanation: A U.S. Army explosive ordnance disposal group. Sponsor of the CJTF Troy deployment. Linked up in OIF I, January to June 2006, at Mosul.
civilian: An Army bomb-disposal headquarters.

name: 16th Engineer Brigade
explanation: A U.S. Army engineer brigade. Sponsor of the CJTF Troy deployment. Linked up in OIF I at FOB Sykes.
civilian: An Army engineer headquarters.

name: 3rd Special Forces Group (Airborne)
explanation: A U.S. Army Special Forces group. Customer on OEF I, at FOB Delaram, while the in-theater command was CJSOTF-A.
civilian: An Army Special Forces unit.

name: 75th Rangers
explanation: The U.S. Army's Ranger regiment. Customer on OEF II, at FOB Orgun-E, while the in-theater command was SOJTF-A.
civilian: An Army Ranger unit.

name: Southeast Regional Calibration Center
explanation: The Navy's Southeast Regional Calibration Center, at Naval Air Station Jacksonville. A calibration center checks the test equipment other commands use. The NEC on this tour is 1589, which matches that work.
civilian: A laboratory that keeps measuring tools honest.

name: Task Force Iron Shield
explanation: Individual-augmentee tour that started in October 2008, after SERCC. Five months at Fort Bliss with HHB 3-3 ADA, then the rest in country at Joint Base Balad. Task Force Iron Shield was the in-theater command. The 11th Air Defense Artillery Brigade was the over-arching parent (admin). HHB 3-3 ADA was the partner. The 332nd Air Expeditionary Wing at Joint Base Balad was the customer. The campaign phase named for this tour is Iraq Sovereignty.
civilian: He was still a sailor, working inside an Army deployment.

name: 11th Air Defense Artillery Brigade
explanation: U.S. Army air-defense brigade at Fort Bliss. Over-arching parent (admin) for the OIF II individual-augmentee tour. HHB 3-3 ADA, of 3rd Battalion, 3rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, fell under this brigade.
civilian: The Army brigade that owned the C-RAM deployment on paper.

name: HHB, 3rd Battalion, 3rd Air Defense Artillery
explanation: Headquarters and Headquarters Battery, 3rd Battalion, 3rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment. Partner on the OIF II individual-augmentee tour: five months of training at Fort Bliss from October 2008, then the rest of the tour in country at Joint Base Balad under Task Force Iron Shield. Fell under 11th ADA.
civilian: The Army air-defense battery that trained with him at Fort Bliss and partnered on the C-RAM tour.

name: 332nd Air Expeditionary Wing
explanation: U.S. Air Force wing at Joint Base Balad. Customer (endpoint) of the OIF II C-RAM tour.
civilian: The Air Force wing the C-RAM mission protected.

name: Joint Communications Support Element
explanation: A joint unit, based at MacDill Air Force Base in Florida, that sends small communications teams out quickly for special operations and other joint commanders. Reported in 2009 and detached in 2014. Made Chief in the last year of this tour, 16 September 2014. The NEC listed for the tour is 9613. It included the two Afghanistan deployments.
civilian: A communications unit made of every branch, not a Navy ship.

name: Combined Joint Special Operations Task Force — Afghanistan
explanation: OEF I in-theater command, 2010–2011, at FOB Delaram, while assigned to JCSE. The customer was an ODA of 3rd Special Forces Group. The role in the record is communications, not service as a special operator. About seven months.
civilian: The headquarters he supported. Being the communicator for that headquarters is not the same job as the operators it commanded.

name: Special Operations Joint Task Force — Afghanistan
explanation: OEF II in-theater command, 2012–2013, at FOB Orgun-E, while assigned to JCSE. The partner was 290th JCSS. The customer was 75th Rangers. The role in the record is communications, not service as a special operator. About seven months.
civilian: The later Afghanistan headquarters he supported.

name: 290th Joint Communications Support Squadron
explanation: Air National Guard communications squadron. Partner (mission enabler) on OEF II only, under SOJTF-A.
civilian: An Air Guard communications unit that worked the same mission.

name: Naval Hospital Jacksonville
explanation: The Navy hospital at Jacksonville, Florida, and the last active-duty command. JCSE ended in 2014. He reported in 2015. Last duty assignment was Naval Hospital Jacksonville, with separation processing at the personnel support detachment on Naval Air Station Jacksonville.
civilian: A hospital, not a ship. An electronics technician there maintains medical and other electronic equipment. The day-to-day job is not further described.

name: EOD Mobile Unit 11
explanation: Partner unit of the CJTF Troy deployment in OIF I, 2006, during the EODMU 5 tour.
open: Minimal record built from command-plates.json and units.json (CJTF Troy). Dates and place not entered.

name: Assault Craft Unit 4
explanation: Exercise partner on the USS Tortuga (LSD-46) TAD, late 1997 into early 1998. It ran the landing craft launched from the ship's well deck.
open: Minimal record built from units.json (USS Tortuga) and supplement.json (PAR-04: ACU 4). Dates and place not entered on the unit.

name: Royal Thai Navy
explanation: Host and partner during Exercise Cobra Gold, 2004 and 2005, at U-Tapao Air Base, Rayong, THA, during the EODMU 5 tour.
open: Minimal record built from command-plates.json. Dates and place not entered on the unit.

name: Australian CDT
explanation: Host and partner during Exercise Talisman Saber, 2005 and 2007, at Camp Growl, Shoalwater Bay, AUS, during the EODMU 5 tour.
open: Minimal record built from command-plates.json. Full name, dates and place not entered on the unit.

name: Afghan National Army (ANA)
explanation: Foreign partner on the JCSE OEF I deployment at FOB Delaram (CJSOTF-A, 2010–2011). Dates and details not entered.
open: Graphic supplied by Sergio (Oct 2026). Blank dates, no map place. Not on the Map.

name: 32nd Light Infantry Battalion, 3rd Infantry Brigade, Georgian Armed Forces
explanation: Foreign partner on the JCSE OEF I deployment at FOB Delaram (CJSOTF-A, 2010–2011).
open: Crest: no 32nd Battalion insignia was found in a public source; the card shows the 3rd Infantry Brigade shoulder badge (Wikimedia Commons, public domain). Dates blank on the card; no map place. Not on the Map.

name: Regimental Combat Team 2 (RCT-2)
explanation: Partner on the JCSE OEF I deployment at FOB Delaram (CJSOTF-A, 2010–2011).
open: Crest: 2nd Marine Regiment insignia (Wikimedia Commons, public domain, USMC). Dates blank on the card; no map place. Not on the Map.

name: Local Hires
explanation: Local hires on the JCSE OEF I deployment at FOB Delaram (CJSOTF-A, 2010–2011). Placeholder card: graphic, dates and details not entered.
